proof_roadmap: The local complete intersection property and the K-theoretic description (proof lines 13882-13896).
difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y a morphism of schemes locally of finite type over (S, delta) with X and Y quasi-compact, regular, of affine diagonal and finite dimension, the lemma asserts that f is local complete intersection and that, assuming the Gysin map exists for f, f^!(alpha . beta) = f^!alpha . f^!beta in CH^*(X) otimes Q for the intersection product of the regular section (statement lines 13867-13880). The first assertion is More on Morphisms, Lemma labelled more-morphisms-lemma-morphism-regular-schemes-is-lci; the proof records f^![Y] = [X] by Lemma labelled lemma-lci-gysin-easy, writes alpha = ch(alpha') cap [Y] and beta = ch(beta') cap [Y] with alpha', beta' in K_0(Vect(X)) otimes Q as in the construction of the product, and sets c = ch(alpha'), c' = ch(beta') so that alpha . beta = c cap c' cap [Y] (proof lines 13882-13896). Since f^! commutes with both c and c' by Lemma labelled lemma-lci-gysin-commutes, a six term chain moves f^! onto the fundamental class and back, giving the multiplicativity (proof lines 13898-13910). Recognising that the regular theory admits the same bivariant bookkeeping as the smooth case, with the Chern character bridging to K-theory, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
